did_you_know.text: The word mum means a physical defect or blemish, and the Torah uses it for animals as well as in other contexts. This emphasizes that an offering must be whole and fit for its purpose.

The phrase “host of heaven” is an ancient expression for the sun, moon, and other heavenly bodies, pictured as an organized army in the sky. In ancient cultures, some peoples worshiped these celestial bodies.

Requiring at least two witnesses helps prevent a conviction based on one person’s story alone. The same principle appears again in Deuteronomy 19:15: “A matter must be established by the testimony of two witnesses.”
The phrase “you shall rise and go up” shows that difficult cases were to be brought before a central court rather than decided locally. In this passage, the central place is not yet named.

In ancient Egypt, horses and chariots were important symbols of military power. The Book of Kings also reports that Solomon imported horses from Egypt, so this warning concerns the danger of relying on foreign military power.
The phrase mishneh ha-Torah can mean a copy or a repetition of the Torah. It also became the traditional Hebrew name of Deuteronomy, because the book repeats and summarizes earlier laws and ideas.
The verse gives the king a test of character: he must lead without feeling superior to his fellow citizens. This remains an important idea today—authority should not make a person arrogant.
